The New York Foundling also employs AI-powered chatbots to streamline administrative tasks and improve client service data entry.

title: Big Oil Faded. Will Big Tech?
summary: This article questions whether Big Tech companies, currently dominant, face a similar fate to Big Oil, specifically Exxon Mobil, which was once the world's most valuable company but has since declined. The author draws parallels between the economic and political influence of past oil superpowers and current tech giants, suggesting that while Big Tech seems invincible now, history shows that even dominant industries can lose relevance due to changing global dynamics and a failure to adapt.

title: Zoom posts another stellar quarter, with revenue up 355 percent
summary: Zoom reported exceptional second-quarter financial results, with revenue soaring 355% year-over-year, significantly surpassing market expectations. This growth is attributed to the widespread shift to remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic and organizations planning for long-term remote operations. The company saw a massive increase in customers and is projecting substantial revenue for the full fiscal year 2021.

title: $217 Million Pour Into Grayscale's Crypto Funds Following Bitcoin TV Ad Campaign
summary: Grayscale Investments reported a significant influx of $217 million into its cryptocurrency funds during the third quarter of 2020, bringing its assets under management (AUM) to over $5.9 billion. This surge in investment is largely attributed to the company's recent Bitcoin TV ad campaign, which aimed to educate mainstream investors about Bitcoin's potential as a store of value. The campaign appears to have successfully attracted institutional investors, as 81% of the investments came from this sector.

title: NVIDIA Delivers Greatest-Ever Generational Leap with GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs, powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivering the most significant generational performance leap in GeForce history with up to 2x the performance and 1.9x the power efficiency of the previous generation. These new GPUs, including the RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070, offer unprecedented real-time ray tracing and AI gaming capabilities, along with new tools like NVIDIA Reflex, Omniverse Machinima, and Broadcast. Fortnite is also integrating RTX real-time ray tracing, enhancing the gaming experience with advanced graphical features.

title: Walmart Takes On Amazon Prime: Membership Program Will Deliver From Stores
summary: Walmart is officially launching Walmart+, an annual membership service priced at $98 per year or $12.95 per month, to compete with Amazon Prime. The program will offer free same-day delivery of groceries and other items from local stores, gas discounts, and mobile checkout, with plans to expand perks. Walmart hopes to leverage its extensive grocery business to attract subscribers, many of whom already use Amazon Prime.

title: Zoom Meetings Demand Leads to Stock Explosion, More Channel Hype
summary: Zoom significantly surpassed its revenue forecasts for Q2 2021, reporting $664 million against expectations of $500 million, and raised its full-year revenue projection to $2.37 billion due to increased demand for its video conferencing services during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's stock price surged by 41% and nearly 700% for the year. Despite this growth, Zoom's approach to its channel partner program, primarily favoring direct sales for Zoom meetings, has prompted discussions among industry analysts about its future channel strategy and potential for further ecosystem development.

title: Bet on Wild Swings in the Market With the SPXL ETF
summary: The Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X Shares (SPXL) ETF is designed for traders to capitalize on short-term market upswings by delivering three times the gains of the S&P 500, using leverage and investing in fast-rising stocks. While it offers significant profit potential during bullish periods, its leveraged nature and daily resets mean it can also lead to rapid losses during downturns, making it suitable only for active trading rather than buy-and-hold strategies. Investors are cautioned about its high expense ratio and the need for close market monitoring due to its volatility.

title: What the future of TikTok means for retail
summary: This article discusses the implications for retailers and brands if TikTok is banned or acquired, particularly in light of a 2020 executive order by then-President Trump. It highlights how brands like e.l.f. Cosmetics have successfully leveraged TikTok for marketing, achieving massive engagement, and emphasizes the need for marketers to have a backup plan and understand alternative platforms if TikTok becomes unavailable. Experts suggest new, similar platforms would emerge and that brands must adapt their content to the aesthetic of whichever platform their target audience, especially Gen Z, uses.

title: Users demand threaded replies to Microsoft Teams messages
summary: Microsoft Teams users are expressing frustration over the lack of a threaded reply feature in the desktop version, a functionality available in competitors like Slack, Webex Teams, and even the mobile version of Teams. Over 28,000 users have voted for this feature on the Teams user feedback forum, with many highlighting its importance for organizing conversations and preventing misunderstandings. While Microsoft is working on other requested features like multiple account access and integrating Tasks, users find the absence of threaded replies a significant drawback.

title: Marvell exits the general purpose Arm server business
summary: Marvell Technology Group has announced it is discontinuing its ThunderX3 Arm-based server processor for general-purpose server use. The company will instead focus on vertical markets and hyperscalers, customizing silicon for major cloud providers. This move allows Marvell to secure up-front commitments and reduce risk by co-funding custom chip development with customers.

title: SAP Supervisory Board Appoints Sabine Bendiek as New Executive Board Member to Lead Human Resources and Operations
summary: SAP SE announced that Sabine Bendiek, Chairwoman of Microsoft Germany's Management Board, has been appointed to the SAP Executive Board. She will join as chief people officer and labor director in early 2021, leading Human Resources and people strategy. By mid-2021, Bendiek will also assume the role of chief operating officer, becoming SAP's first chief people and operating officer, focusing on driving business-centric HR and operational efficiency alongside digital transformation.

title: Sabine Bendiek: The New SAP Executive Board Member and CPO
summary: SAP has announced Sabine Bendiek as a new Executive Board member and Chief People Officer and Labor Director, effective early next year. Bendiek previously served as Managing Director of Microsoft Germany, where she significantly boosted the company's cloud-based business. Her appointment is seen as a strategic move to focus on talent attraction, employee development, and leadership culture, especially as SAP navigates the evolving economic landscape and technological shifts like cloud computing and cybersecurity.

title: Tech Mahindra Launches Dedicated ‘Microsoft Business Unit’ to Accelerate Digital Transformation Globally
summary: Tech Mahindra has launched a dedicated 'Microsoft Business Unit' to accelerate digital transformation journeys globally. This new unit will focus on developing enterprise cloud solutions leveraging Microsoft platforms and technologies, including Azure, Dynamics 365, and Microsoft 365. It aims to amplify Tech Mahindra's collaboration with Microsoft and cater to the dynamic needs of customers across various sectors.

title: Freight Transportation Management System Market Update - See How Industry Players are Preparing against Covid-19 depression
summary: This article announces a comprehensive research document by AMA Research on the Freight Transportation Management System (TMS) market. The report details growth factors, strategies, and segmentation across regions, while also highlighting market trends, drivers, restraints, and challenges. Key players like The Descartes Systems Group Inc., Oracle Corporation, and SAP are featured, and the study also addresses the impact of Covid-19 on the industry.

title: Microsoft and Akamai hack together to save the planet
summary: Microsoft and Akamai Technologies collaborated during the Microsoft Akamai Sustainability Hack (MASH) to develop an app aimed at helping individuals calculate, track, and reduce their carbon footprint, specifically focusing on food consumption. The app incorporates gamification elements, computer vision, and object detection APIs to engage users and encourage sustainable choices. The hackathon successfully demonstrated the power of virtual collaboration, allowing team members from different locations to contribute to a shared goal of environmental impact reduction.

title: Government Could See More Cloud Computing Adoption
summary: Government organizations are increasingly adopting cloud computing, a trend accelerated by the Covid-19 pandemic. This shift could drive interest in cloud computing exchange-traded funds (ETFs) such as the Global X Cloud Computing ETF (Nasdaq: CLOU) and the WisdomTree Cloud Computing Fund (WCLD). The article highlights how widespread cloud adoption by public and private sectors has been growing, with Covid-19 acting as a catalyst.

title: Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund Review: Should You Invest?
summary: This article reviews the Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund, which invests in Schroder International Selection Fund Global Equity Alpha. The author discusses the underlying fund's performance against its benchmark, highlighting a poor track record and high expense ratios, especially for the regular plan. The article concludes by recommending investors consider alternatives with lower expenses, such as the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund, for international diversification.

title: Network Security Firm Qualys Floats to Top of Cloud Computing
summary: Qualys, a network security firm founded in 1999, is positioned for significant growth in the cloud computing sector, serving nearly 40 Fortune 100 companies among its 4,000 customers. The company, known for its vulnerability assessment and credit card database security, offers the advantage of instantly adding new services and scaling based on customer needs without major capital expenditure. Qualys reinvests 25% of its revenue into R&D and has successfully navigated market challenges as a software-as-a-service pioneer.

title: QualysGuard Patch Report Aligns IT Security with Operations
summary: Qualys announced a new Patch Report feature within QualysGuard Vulnerability Management, designed to provide actionable patching information for non-security IT staff. This report offers prioritized lists of necessary patches to reduce risk efficiently. Joe Bennett of CredAbility praised the new feature for improving vulnerability remediation and tracking patch effectiveness, with support for Microsoft and Adobe patches already included.

title: Oracle on Google Cloud: Two Deployment Options
summary: This article discusses two primary deployment options for running Oracle on Google Cloud: using partner-managed Oracle instances available on the Google Cloud Marketplace, and setting up a custom Oracle instance via Google's Bare Metal Solution. It outlines the pros and cons of each method, noting that Google Cloud Platform does not directly support running Oracle in a virtual instance due to licensing limitations. NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP is also presented as a solution for enterprise-level Oracle deployments on GCP.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Seth Klarman, Steve Cohen, Ken Griffin, Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), Khiron Life Sciences Corp (KHRNF), and More
summary: This article provides a roundup of recent hedge fund and insider trading news, featuring prominent figures like Seth Klarman, Steve Cohen, and Ken Griffin. Key highlights include Klarman's donation to Spelman College, Cohen's pending acquisition of the New York Mets, and Griffin's significant political donation, alongside details on ESG investing trends and notable insider stock transactions involving Microsoft (MSFT) and Khiron Life Sciences Corp (KHRNF).

title: New life for old corporate computers so students can learn from home - Microsoft Stories Asia
summary: Microsoft, in partnership with corporate groups and non-profits in Hong Kong, is giving old corporate computers new life by refurbishing them and distributing them to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. This initiative addresses the challenges of remote learning during the COVID-19 pandemic, where many students lack proper devices for online education. The program, involving organizations like the Crossroads Foundation and the Association of IT Leaders in Education, aims to ensure that students have the necessary tools for effective blended learning and improved academic performance.

title: HR Technology Highlights; Featuring Limeade, ServiceNow, Zimit
summary: This article provides a round-up of HR technology news, focusing on solutions that help HR teams manage a smooth return to the office and optimize HR tech for employee safety and productivity during the Covid-19 pandemic. It highlights new platform innovations from companies like Limeade and ServiceNow, and features a quote on the importance of data and analytics in HR. The piece also includes an expert Q&A on assessment implementation and a list of top HR-related articles.

title: TikTok data could be gold mine for ERP, HR systems
summary: TikTok's vast user data and its powerful AI-driven recommendation engine could be highly valuable for enterprise resource planning (ERP) and human resources (HR) systems, attracting interest from companies like Microsoft and Oracle. This data could offer insights into consumer trends, improve advertising integration, and enhance job matching capabilities. The potential acquisition of TikTok's U.S. operations by a U.S. company could alleviate governmental concerns about data ownership by China.

title: Werner Edge with Microsoft Azure offers safety and savings
summary: Werner Enterprises has partnered with Microsoft Azure to develop "Werner Edge," a cloud-based platform designed to enhance safety and achieve cost savings. The system integrates telematics and video event data, automatically parsing critical events to improve driver coaching and reduce false positives, significantly speeding up the safety event review process. Werner is also rolling out new telematics systems with real-time coaching alerts and developing features for trip planning and load management to further optimize operations.

title: Using Foreign Funds to Correct for a Sliding Dollar
summary: The dollar has recently been in decline relative to other foreign currencies, primarily due to low interest rates and a shift in the Fed's monetary policy. This can have varying implications for investors' portfolios depending on their holdings. Foreign stock and bond funds, particularly unhedged ones, can benefit from a weaker dollar, while U.S. companies with significant foreign revenue may also see improved profits.

title: AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T) Decides To Retain Video Game Business Of Warner Bros
summary: AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T) has decided to retain the video game business of Warner Bros., reversing an earlier decision to sell it, citing its value and potential for future revenue. The company had initially considered divesting the unit to help pay down debt but now sees its potential, especially with upcoming game releases like a new Harry Potter title. Despite engaging advisors for the sale earlier in the year, a leadership change at AT&T contributed to the decision to keep the gaming division.

title: Capital One and Microsoft team up to fight fraud at the point of sale
summary: Capital One and Microsoft have partnered to combat fraud at the point of sale by improving the sharing of transaction data between merchants and card issuers. This collaboration, leveraging Microsoft Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection and Capital One's Enhanced Decisioning Data API, aims to reduce false-positive declines, increase transaction acceptance rates for valid purchases, and enhance customer protection from fraud. The initiative is particularly critical with the rise of online spending and associated fraud threats.

title: Microsoft appoints Clare Barclay as Chief Executive Officer, Microsoft UK
summary: Microsoft has announced the appointment of Clare Barclay as the new Chief Executive Officer for Microsoft UK, effective October 1, 2020. Barclay, currently the Chief Operating Officer, will succeed Cindy Rose, who will transition to President for Microsoft's Western Europe business. Rose previously led Microsoft UK for four years and will now oversee operations across 14 countries.

title: Turtle Beach Recon 70 gaming headset review: Versatile & wallet-friendly
summary: The Turtle Beach Recon 70 gaming headset offers versatile cross-platform compatibility and a budget-friendly price point of $39.95, making it suitable for current and next-gen consoles as well as mobile and PC. While it delivers standard features like a flip-to-mute mic and a lightweight design, it prioritizes functionality and comfort over premium audio features such as spatial sound or deep bass. The review concludes that it's an excellent value headset for gamers on a budget or for dual virtual schooling and gaming use.

title: Tractor Supply Company Joins the American Connection Project Broadband Coalition With a $1 Million Donation Initiative to Help Close Digital Divide in Rural America
summary: Tractor Supply Company announced its partnership with the American Connection Project Broadband Coalition, pledging up to $1 million to help close the digital divide in rural America. This initiative includes a $1 donation for every app download, offering free high-speed internet in select store parking lots, and donating 3,000 Chromebooks to employees' children. This effort aims to address the critical need for internet connectivity for business, healthcare, and education in rural communities, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: New supercomputer announced
summary: Microsoft has unveiled one of the world's top five publicly disclosed supercomputers, making its infrastructure available in Azure for OpenAI to train massive artificial intelligence models. This initiative aims to create a platform for other organizations and developers, enabling the creation of new AI applications that leverage supercomputing capabilities and high-bandwidth networks. Microsoft Chief Technical Officer Kevin Scott believes this will lead to hard-to-imagine new applications.

title: Russian Intelligence Hackers Are Back, Microsoft Warns, Aiming at Officials of Both Parties (Published 2020)
summary: Microsoft has warned that Russian military intelligence hackers, previously responsible for the Democratic National Committee attack, are targeting campaign staff, consultants, and think tanks associated with both Democrats and Republicans with new, stealthier methods. This assessment follows a whistle-blower claim about suppressed intelligence regarding Russian interference. While Microsoft also found Chinese and Iranian hacker activity, the Chinese attacks were primarily focused on Biden campaign staff members' private email accounts and other prominent individuals, potentially complicating previous government assessments.

title: EBay founder Pierre Omidyar steps down from board
summary: EBay founder Pierre Omidyar has stepped down from the company's board of directors, becoming a director emeritus. Jesse Cohn of Elliott Management also left the board as part of a broader overhaul. EBay announced two new board members and reported strong financial performance for the first half of the year due to increased online shopping during the pandemic.

title: Our Ecosystem of Technology Partners for Federal Agencies
summary: ICF highlights its extensive ecosystem of technology partners dedicated to accelerating modernization efforts and integrating cutting-edge capabilities for federal agencies. These strategic partnerships enable ICF to deliver tailored, scalable solutions that enhance operational efficiency, ensure secure transformation, and drive measurable impact, particularly in areas like AI advancement. The article underscores how these partnerships facilitate high-impact, interoperable industry solutions that streamline processes and improve service delivery for various sectors including U.S. federal government, health, utilities, and energy markets.

title: Inside Adobe’s employee-focused COVID-19 response roadmap
summary: Adobe successfully transitioned its 22,000+ global workforce to remote work within a single weekend during the COVID-19 crisis, leveraging previous contingency planning experience and existing cloud infrastructure. The company prioritized employee experience by enhancing collaboration tools, implementing a Zero-Trust Enterprise Network (ZEN) for secure access, and providing "desktop as a service" solutions. This focus on employee well-being and productivity ensured business continuity and a smooth transition to long-term remote work.

title: FedEx senses need for real-time parcel tracking
summary: FedEx is introducing SenseAware ID, a new sensor-based logistics device for real-time parcel tracking, particularly aimed at critical shipments like eventual COVID-19 vaccine deliveries. This initiative is part of FedEx's broader strategy to enhance its global shipping experience and improve safety and timeliness in response to increasing delivery demands. The technology will initially be rolled out for First Overnight shipments in the U.S. and expanded to more customers in 2021.

title: ByteDance chooses Oracle over Microsoft for TikTok's US operations
summary: ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese parent company, has selected Oracle as its U.S. technology partner, rejecting Microsoft's bid to acquire TikTok's U.S. operations. This decision comes as the Trump administration threatened to ban TikTok over national security concerns related to its Chinese ownership. Oracle confirmed its joint bid with ByteDance to the Treasury Department.

title: Oracle confirms it will partner with TikTok after Microsoft's bid rejected
summary: Oracle has confirmed it will partner with TikTok after Microsoft's bid was rejected, as the video-sharing app works to avoid a ban by the Trump administration. The deal faces hurdles including securing approval from both US and Chinese authorities, especially given recent changes to China's export rules regarding AI technology. The nature of the partnership is unclear, with reports suggesting it could be a restructuring rather than a full sale, and the key algorithm's inclusion in any deal remains a point of contention.

title: How Oracle, now partnering with TikTok, became the Trump administration’s favorite tech company.
summary: The article details how Oracle became the Trump administration's preferred tech company, culminating in its partnership with TikTok over Microsoft. It highlights Oracle's strong ties to Trump through its co-founder Larry Ellison and CEO Safra Catz, who supported his reelection campaign. The article also describes instances where the White House sided with Oracle in legal disputes and controversies, like the Google lawsuit and the JEDI contract, and Oracle's involvement during the coronavirus pandemic.

title: EA eliminating Origin brand with new EA Desktop app
summary: Electronic Arts is replacing its Origin platform with a new "EA Desktop" app, aiming to provide a faster and more convenient PC gaming experience. The change also involves "doubling down" on the EA Play and EA Play Pro subscription services, allowing players to access games as long as they maintain their subscription. This overhaul comes as Origin developed a reputation for being slow and cumbersome since its 2011 launch, and follows EA's recent move to bring its PC titles to Steam.

title: What the heck is going on with TikTok and Oracle, explained
summary: The article explains the complex situation surrounding TikTok's potential deal with Oracle, following an executive order from President Trump mandating a sale of TikTok's US operations due to national security concerns. Instead of a full acquisition, Oracle is proposing to become a "trusted technology provider," raising questions about how this addresses the initial security concerns and the role of Oracle's leadership's ties to the Trump administration. The deal's specifics are still unclear, leaving many to wonder about the future of TikTok in the US.

title: ByteDance seeks Oracle partnership to avoid US TikTok sale
summary: ByteDance is pursuing a partnership deal with Oracle for TikTok's US operations, aiming to avoid a forced sale amidst US government concerns over data security; Microsoft's previous bid was rejected. This new proposal involves Oracle managing TikTok's US user data on its cloud servers, but the deal's structure and the fate of TikTok's valuable algorithm remain uncertain, requiring approval from both US and Chinese governments. Analysts suggest that without the core algorithm included, a full sale of TikTok's US business seems unlikely, potentially leading to a shutdown in the US.

title: The Oracle-TikTok Deal Sure Worked Out Well for a Close Trump Ally
summary: Oracle secured a deal to become TikTok's "trusted tech partner" in the U.S., beating out Microsoft, a move that requires White House approval. This agreement is viewed critically due to Oracle's close ties with the Trump administration, including co-founder Larry Ellison hosting a fundraiser and CEO Safra Catz serving on Trump's transition team. The article suggests these connections may have strategically influenced the outcome of the deal amid Trump's earlier threats to ban TikTok.

title: -ByteDance picks Oracle as partner to try to save TikTok U.S.
summary: ByteDance has chosen Oracle as its technology partner to keep TikTok operating in the United States, sidestepping an outright sale but structuring the deal as a partnership. This decision comes after intense pressure from the U.S. government, with Oracle expected to manage TikTok's U.S. user data and potentially acquire a stake in its U.S. operations. The proposal will undergo review by the U.S. Treasury Department and CFIUS to address national security concerns.

title: Microsoft retrieves Project Natick from the North Sea
summary: Microsoft has successfully retrieved its Project Natick underwater data center from the North Sea after a two-year experiment. The project demonstrates the reliability, practicality, and sustainability of underwater data centers, confirming that they can provide increased local connectivity, utilize cheap real estate on the ocean floor, and benefit from energy-efficient cooling. Microsoft is now considering how to scale this technology to support its Azure cloud services.

title: Bill Gates: COVID-19 Has Worsened Inequity in Nearly Every Way
summary: Bill Gates stated that the COVID-19 pandemic has significantly exacerbated social and economic inequality globally, reversing progress made towards the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. The report from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation highlights how the pandemic has stalled efforts to end poverty and hunger, pushing nearly 37 million more people into extreme poverty. Gates emphasized that the pandemic reinforces the importance of these global goals despite setting back progress in areas like education, pay, and healthcare access.

title: The Cloud pioneers
summary: UBS is undergoing a significant digital transformation by adopting a hybrid cloud strategy, aiming to move a third of its applications to on-premises private cloud solutions, a third to the public cloud, and a third remaining on mainframe infrastructure by 2022. This migration has already shown benefits like reduced setup times and increased stability for platforms like UBS Neo, with a goal to enhance business features and accelerate growth. The company is actively investing in new cloud-native applications and equipping its teams with the necessary skills for this journey.

title: Oracle, TikTok deal decision imminent
summary: The U.S. government is close to making a decision on Oracle's "trusted tech partnership" deal with TikTok, with an announcement possible as early as Tuesday evening or Wednesday. The Treasury Department's Committee On Foreign Investment in the U.S. (CFIUS) is meeting with ByteDance officials to review if the deal meets national security standards, amid ongoing concerns about data security and Chinese government influence. While some officials favor the Oracle approach as an expedient solution, others express reservations due to it not fully removing Chinese involvement in TikTok's U.S. operations.

title: bp and Microsoft form strategic partnership to drive digital energy ‎innovation and advance net zero goals
summary: BP and Microsoft have announced a strategic partnership to drive digital energy innovation and advance their net-zero carbon goals. The collaboration involves co-innovation on digital solutions, BP's continued use of Microsoft Azure cloud services, and BP supplying renewable energy to help Microsoft meet its 2025 renewable energy targets. This partnership aims to leverage the expertise of both companies to achieve their decarbonization ambitions and support others in reducing carbon emissions.

title: Stock ETFs Gain Amid Positive Economic Data And Tech Rebound
summary: Stock index ETFs and individual stocks rallied on Tuesday, September 15, 2020, driven by a rebound in tech stocks, positive economic data from China and the U.S., and optimism surrounding coronavirus vaccine trials. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite all advanced, with tech giants like Apple, Microsoft, Netflix, and Facebook leading the gains, while the banking sector lagged. Analysts have also raised the year-end target for the S&P 500 due to tech mergers and sector excitement.

title: New Upwork Study Finds 36% of the U.S. Workforce Freelance Amid the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: A new study by Upwork, "Freelance Forward: 2020", reveals that 36% of the U.S. workforce, or 59 million Americans, freelanced in the past year, contributing $1.2 trillion to the economy. This growth was spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic, with an influx of young, highly-skilled first-time freelancers seeking flexible work. Many freelancers reported increased earning potential and improved coping mechanisms during the pandemic compared to traditional employees.

title: Global Audio and Video Editing Software Market- Featuring Acon AS, Adobe Inc., Animoto Inc., and Apple Inc. Among Others
summary: The global audio and video editing software market is projected to grow by USD 2.5 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR exceeding 11%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing rate of content generation and a shift towards cloud-based delivery models. The report provides a comprehensive analysis including market sizing, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis, covering companies such as Adobe Inc., Apple Inc., and Microsoft Corp.

title: Snowflake Stock: What You Need to Know About Tech’s Hottest IPO
summary: Snowflake Inc., a data-managing firm founded in 2012, has become Silicon Valley's hottest new public company. It helps companies like Capital One and Electronic Arts manage and analyze data stored on cloud services from providers such as Amazon and Microsoft. The company stated in its IPO filing that it is competing in a market valued at over $80 billion.

title: Here’s who made a killing from Snowflake’s blockbuster IPO
summary: Snowflake's initial public offering resulted in significant gains for various investors and executives. Iconiq Capital saw its 12% stake, purchased for $245 million, surge to over $8.3 billion, while key executives amassed stakes worth $3.7 billion. Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway also made a substantial investment, which doubled in value by lunchtime.

title: -Trump says Oracle close to TikTok deal as ByteDance aims for majority ownership
summary: President Trump indicated that Oracle Corp was nearing a deal for TikTok, despite ByteDance's proposal to retain majority ownership of the popular short video app. ByteDance sought to establish TikTok's headquarters in the U.S. and make Oracle its technology partner and a minority stakeholder, while Trump's administration considered whether to approve the deal amid national security concerns. The proposed deal also faced scrutiny regarding ByteDance's refusal to make payments to the U.S. government and China's stance on technology transfer.

title: ZWIFT RAISES $450 MILLION INVESTMENT; SERIES C ROUND LED BY KKR
summary: Zwift, the online fitness platform, announced a $450 million minority investment led by KKR, with additional investors including Permira, Specialized Bicycle Components’ venture capital fund, Zone 5 Ventures, and the Amazon Alexa Fund. The funding will be used to accelerate the development of Zwift’s core software platform and bring Zwift-designed hardware to market, enhancing the user experience. The company plans to expand its global presence in the at-home gamified fitness subscription business and invest in product innovation and headcount.

title: Small Tech Stocks Soar as the Future Arrives Early (Published 2020)
summary: Smaller technology companies specializing in software, streaming, security, and e-commerce are experiencing significant stock market gains, mirroring the performance of tech giants. This surge is attributed to the accelerated adoption of remote work and online services during the coronavirus pandemic. Experts note an unprecedented shift in workforce dynamics, suggesting these trends will continue to drive the growth of these smaller tech firms.

title: Introducing the Forrester Wave for CCaaS 2020
summary: Forrester's latest Wave report for CCaaS in 2020 evaluated 10 key providers based on 33 criteria, identifying leaders, strong performers, and contenders. Five9, Talkdesk, Genesys, and NICE inContact were named leaders, highlighting their strengths in areas like WFO technology, global deployments, and innovative roadmaps. The report serves as a guide for companies considering new purchases in the contact center as a service market.

title: Turtle Beach's New Stealth 700 Gen 2 And Stealth 600 Gen 2 Headsets For Xbox One, Xbox Series X | S, PlayStation 4, And PlayStation 5 Available At Retail This Sunday, September 20, 2020
summary: Turtle Beach announced the retail availability of its new Stealth 700 Gen 2 and Stealth 600 Gen 2 gaming headsets for Xbox and PlayStation, starting September 20, 2020. These next-generation wireless headsets are designed for both current and upcoming consoles, offering enhanced performance, comfort, and features. The new models aim to continue the success of their predecessors as best-selling wireless gaming headsets.

title: Epic is not EXACTly the Microsoft of Madison
summary: This article argues that while Epic Systems Corp. is often compared to Microsoft in terms of its regional economic impact, the comparison is flawed. The author, through Erik Iverson of WARF, suggests that Exact Sciences, due to its publicly traded nature and broad employee stock options, is more akin to Madison's Microsoft, creating localized wealth. The article also details Epic's private stock plan for employees, noting its differences from Microsoft's early model.

title: The new TikTok-Oracle company named ‘TikTok Global’ plans to go public in a year
summary: TikTok plans to form a new U.S. company with Oracle Corp. called TikTok Global, which aims to hold an initial public offering within approximately a year. The deal is a result of Trump administration concerns over TikTok's Chinese ownership and involves Oracle acquiring a minority stake in the new entity, which will be headquartered in the U.S. with an independent board and strict data security provisions to protect American user data.

title: Parque Eólico Los Teros I de YPF Luz ya inyecta energía renovable al sistema
summary: YPF Luz's Los Teros I wind farm in Azul, Argentina, has begun supplying renewable energy to the national grid after receiving commercial authorization from Cammesa for 99.58 MW from 26 wind turbines. This first phase of the project, with a total investment of $200 million, will eventually reach 123 MW and generate clean energy for 228,000 homes. The park aims to provide renewable energy to major industrial clients and significantly reduce CO2 emissions.

title: IBM Remains America’s Worst Big Tech Company
summary: Despite a change in CEO, IBM continues to underperform significantly compared to other major tech companies, with its stock price declining while competitors surge. The company has experienced nearly six years of revenue decline and its cloud operations show minimal growth, placing it outside the top 50 American companies by market capitalization. IBM lacks strong consumer-focused products and its key brands like Watson and The Weather Channel fail to provide compelling growth engines, indicating a dim future for its return to the top tier of tech.

title: Oracle (ORCL) Trading Lower After TikTok Download Ban
summary: Oracle (ORCL) stock is trading lower after the U.S. Commerce Department banned TikTok and WeChat downloads, effective Sunday. The announcement creates uncertainty around Oracle's potential deal for TikTok's U.S. operations, with the stock needing to hold the $57 to $57.50 price zone to maintain a bullish technical outlook. Long-term patterns suggest only modest upside even if a deal is finalized, and a failed deal could trigger a bearish double top pattern.

title: U.S. Department of Labor and Microsoft Corp. Enter Agreement to Resolve Alleged Hiring Discrimination Affecting 1,229 Applicants in Four States
summary: The U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) and Microsoft Corp. U.S. have reached an agreement to resolve alleged hiring discrimination practices affecting 1,229 applicants in four states. Microsoft will pay $3 million in back pay and interest to these applicants, who experienced hiring disparities based on race and ethnicity for various positions from 2012 to 2018. This resolution stems from OFCCP's Early Resolution Procedures, allowing Microsoft to avoid future evaluations for five years by proactively addressing compliance.

title: Insight Hires Dell’s Ex-Channel Chief Mullen For Dell Sales Blitz
summary: Insight Enterprises has appointed Joyce Mullen, Dell Technologies' former global channel leader, as president of its North American business. Mullen, a 21-year Dell veteran, will officially start her new role on October 26th with a base salary of $600,000. Her extensive experience leading Dell's $50 billion channel organization is expected to boost Insight as it is already a significant Dell partner.

title: Dell’s Joyce Mullen Jumps To Insight: 5 Big Things To Know
summary: Joyce Mullen, former worldwide global channel chief at Dell Technologies, has joined Insight Enterprises as the new North American President. Her compensation package could exceed $5 million in her first year, and her role is expected to influence Insight's sales with key vendors like Dell. Mullen's 21-year career at Dell and expertise in channel, OEM, and distribution are highlighted, alongside her motivations for moving to a smaller company.

title: Air Travel Post COVID-19
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the aviation industry, necessitating a reimagining of air travel focused on passenger safety and comfort. This article highlights how airports are integrating emerging technologies and re-designing the passenger journey to create a more autonomous, safe, and efficient experience, emphasizing seamless digital transactions, enhanced hygiene, and personalized services. Wipro has collaborated with global airports to implement these digital solutions, aiming to improve passenger satisfaction and foster a resilient operating environment for the new normal in aviation.

title: ESG sees record inflows amid pandemic. One leading issuer on the theme's staying power
summary: ESG investing has seen record inflows in 2020, with over $19 billion flowing into ESG ETFs, bringing the total to over $40 billion. Luke Oliver of DWS Group attributes this growth to investors adopting ESG as a core portfolio strategy, noting that ESG companies are often better prepared for future challenges. The trend is fueled by increased awareness of environmental and social issues, along with a shift away from sectors like fossil fuels.

title: TikTok Ban Averted: Trump Gives Oracle-Walmart Deal His 'Blessing'
summary: President Trump has tentatively approved a deal involving Oracle and Walmart to keep TikTok operational in the U.S., averting a ban set for midnight, Sunday. The agreement aims to address national security concerns regarding American user data, even though Chinese company ByteDance is expected to retain a majority ownership stake. This deal is expected to boost Oracle's cloud computing business and allow Walmart to integrate e-commerce into the app.

title: Trump signs off on TikTok deal with Oracle, Walmart
summary: President Trump has approved in concept a deal for TikTok to partner with Oracle and Walmart, making the Chinese-owned video-sharing app a U.S.-based company. This agreement led to a delay in the U.S. ban on TikTok downloads and updates, with Oracle and Walmart acquiring stakes in the new entity, TikTok Global, which plans an IPO within a year. The deal aims to address national security concerns and involves a $5 billion educational fund and significant tax contributions to the U.S. Treasury.

title: -Illumina to buy Jeff Bezos-backed cancer testing firm Grail in $8 bln deal
summary: Illumina announced its plan to acquire Grail Inc., a cancer screening startup backed by investors including Jeff Bezos, in an $8 billion cash-and-stock deal. Grail is developing a liquid biopsy test for early cancer detection, a field Illumina's CEO sees as critical for genomics in the coming decade. Despite the strategic fit, Illumina's shares fell following the announcement, with some analysts questioning the timing of acquiring a company still in critical clinical development stages.

title: The 2020 Enterprise Architecture Awards
summary: The 2020 Forrester and InfoWorld Enterprise Architecture Awards highlight organizations demonstrating strategic leadership and concrete business impact through EA. The winners—CSL Behring, Thomas Jefferson University and Jefferson Health, Lexmark, Sun Life, and Verizon Communications—showcased value in business relationships, digital transformation vision, and effective governance, including responses to the global pandemic. Each company's EA team presented compelling case studies of best practices, ranging from technology platform modernization and governance frameworks to responding to increased demands during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Microsoft to Acquire ZeniMax Media and Its Game Publisher Bethesda Softworks
summary: Microsoft announced its plan to acquire ZeniMax Media, the parent company of Bethesda Softworks, for $7.5 billion in cash. This acquisition significantly boosts Microsoft's gaming division by adding critically acclaimed franchises like The Elder Scrolls and Fallout, increasing its creative studio teams from 15 to 23, and bringing Bethesda's future games to Xbox Game Pass on launch day. The deal aims to further Microsoft's strategy of empowering gamers with diverse content on any device, strengthening Xbox Game Pass, which has surpassed 15 million subscribers.

title: Illumina will pay $8B to acquire Grail, the Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos-backed cancer detection company
summary: Illumina has announced its acquisition of Grail, a cancer detection startup backed by Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos, for $8 billion in cash and stock. Grail, which was spun out of Illumina, had been preparing for an IPO and plans to launch a multi-cancer early detection test in 2021. The news led to an over 8% drop in Illumina's shares on Monday.

title: Uncertainty hangs over shape of TikTok sale to US investors
summary: Uncertainty surrounds the planned sale of TikTok to US investors, with ByteDance stating it will retain a majority stake, contradicting statements from Oracle and Walmart. This discrepancy arises amidst pressure from the Trump administration for a deal over national security concerns, with the final ownership structure and valuation still debated despite a conceptual approval from President Trump.

title: T-Mobile Gets Down to Business for Small Business, Launches New Small Business Plans with Microsoft 365
summary: T-Mobile is launching new rate plans for small businesses, including Microsoft 365 at no extra charge, alongside expanded support teams and updated retail locations. This initiative aims to assist small businesses, which are crucial to the economy, by providing essential productivity tools and enhanced customer service, especially in light of the challenges faced in 2020. T-Mobile highlights its commitment to value, network superiority, and customer satisfaction for businesses of all sizes.

title: COVID-19 Recovery Analysis: Automotive Software
summary: Technavio reports that the automotive software market is expected to grow by $10.70 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR exceeding 9%, despite the COVID-19 pandemic. This growth is primarily driven by the increased adoption of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) in mass-produced vehicles. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, drivers, and the competitive landscape, highlighting key market participants and potential challenges like increasing software complexity.

title: Microsoft (MSFT) to Buy ZeniMax in All-Cash Deal Worth $7.5B
summary: Microsoft announced its plan to acquire ZeniMax Media, parent company of Bethesda Softworks, in an all-cash deal worth $7.5 billion. This acquisition is expected to significantly boost Microsoft's Xbox Game Pass subscriber base and strengthen its position in the video game market against rivals like Sony and Nintendo. The deal comes amidst a growing video games market, driven by cloud gaming, 5G deployment, AR/VR, and COVID-19 induced stay-at-home trends.

title: Analog Devices Collaborates with Microsoft to Mass Produce State-of-the-Art 3D Imaging Products and Solutions
summary: Analog Devices (ADI) has announced a strategic collaboration with Microsoft to mass produce advanced 3D imaging products and solutions, utilizing Microsoft’s 3D time-of-flight (ToF) sensor technology. This partnership aims to deliver high-performance 3D solutions with enhanced depth accuracy for various applications including Industry 4.0, automotive, gaming, and augmented reality. ADI will design, manufacture, and sell a new series of 3D ToF imagers and systems, with the first products expected to release by the end of 2020.

title: Introducing Azure Orbital: Process Satellite Data At Cloud-Scale + SES Signs On…
summary: Microsoft has launched Azure Orbital, a new ground station service that integrates satellite operations directly with Azure’s cloud platform, enabling satellite operators to control satellites, process data, and scale operations. This service aims to address global challenges by leveraging cloud capabilities for vast amounts of data from space. SES has partnered with Microsoft, selecting Azure Orbital to collocate ground stations for its next-generation O3b mPOWER communication system, streamlining operations and accelerating digital transformation.

title: Oracle is a distant laggard in cloud infrastructure market even after TikTok deal
summary: Despite recent high-profile customer wins like TikTok and Zoom, Oracle remains a "niche player" in the cloud infrastructure market, significantly trailing leaders Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Gartner estimates Oracle's market share at around 2%, and analysts note that its growth is still heavily reliant on traditional database software, with its stock performance lagging behind major cloud competitors. The TikTok deal, while a "shot in the arm," is viewed by some analysts as politically motivated rather than a testament to Oracle's competitive cloud capabilities.

title: Beijing unlikely to approve Oracle, Walmart's TikTok deal - Global Times
summary: A state-backed Chinese newspaper, Global Times, reported that Beijing is unlikely to approve the deal struck by Oracle Corp and Walmart Inc with ByteDance regarding TikTok. The newspaper characterized the deal as "unfair" and catering to "unreasonable demands" from Washington, potentially harming China's national security and dignity. China's government has largely refrained from direct comments, though the foreign ministry has advocated for a fair environment for foreign companies.

title: HubSpot CRM gets enterprise makeover
summary: HubSpot has introduced a revamped Sales Hub Enterprise CRM, aiming to scale with growing businesses and appeal to larger organizations, including prospective Salesforce customers. The new offering includes advanced reporting, CPQ, and integrations with systems like LinkedIn Navigator and various accounting platforms. Analyst Liz Miller notes that this move positions HubSpot to compete more directly in the enterprise market by filling functional gaps while leveraging its existing reputation as a user-friendly tool for small and midmarket businesses.

title: AT&T and Microsoft to streamline cloud connectivity for IoT devices worldwide
summary: AT&T and Microsoft are partnering to streamline cloud connectivity for Internet of Things (IoT) devices globally. They are launching an integrated IoT solution featuring an AT&T-powered guardian device with Azure Sphere, enabling businesses to securely connect machines to the cloud without relying on public internet or third-party Wi-Fi. This collaboration aims to simplify massive IoT deployments, improve security, and help various industries transform operations.

title: Securing Remote Work: Prisma Access and Prisma Cloud With Azure AD
summary: This article discusses the integration of Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access and Prisma Cloud with Microsoft Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) to secure remote workforces. It highlights the challenges of traditional VPNs in hybrid environments and explains how the combined solution provides identity- and policy-driven secure access, conditional access, and continuous monitoring for users across diverse locations and cloud platforms. The integrations were slated for customer availability in October 2020.

title: ClassEDU Launches to Bring "Class for Zoom" Product to Market to Help Millions of Teachers and Students Learning Online Due To COVID
summary: ClassEDU Inc. announced its launch and secured $16 million in seed financing to bring its "Class for Zoom" product to market. This platform aims to enhance online learning by adding features like attendance tracking, assignment distribution, and quizzes to Zoom, making virtual classrooms feel more like in-person ones. The funding round saw participation from key Zoom investors and prominent education leaders, recognizing the critical need for improved remote learning solutions hastened by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Investing in the Nasdaq-100: Why an Equal-Weight Version Presents a Tactical Choice
summary: This article discusses the benefits and considerations of investing in an equal-weighted Nasdaq-100 (NDXE) compared to the traditional market-cap-weighted Nasdaq-100 (NDX). It highlights how NDXE offers reduced concentration in mega-cap firms and the Technology sector, providing a tactical choice given historical turnover among market leaders. The article also compares NDXE's performance and volatility with NDX and the S&P 500 equal-weighted index (SPW).

title: Is the VGS ETF the best for passive investing?
summary: This article examines the Vanguard MSCI Index International Shares ETF (ASX: VGS) as a strong option for passive investing due to its broad diversification across over 1,500 businesses in major developed countries. It highlights VGS's sector allocation, top holdings including tech giants, and its average annual return of 9.65% over the past five years. The piece concludes that while VGS offers good diversification, investors should consider its management fee compared to other ETFs and explore various options for growth and dividends.

title: Future of Sales 2025: Why B2B Sales Needs a Digital-First Approach
summary: The article discusses the accelerated shift towards digital-first B2B sales, predicting that by 2025, 80% of sales interactions will occur in digital channels. It emphasizes the need for sales leaders to adopt a digital mindset, diversify digital selling tools, and rethink sales enablement to cater to evolving customer buying preferences. The transformation necessitates adaptive systems to optimize digital interactions and maintain relevance.

title: Vitality: Delivering a valuable experience for customers
summary: Vitality, founded in 2004, distinguishes itself in the insurance market by integrating wellness into its offerings, aiming to improve customers' lives and encouraging 100 million people to be 20% more active by 2025. Chief Digital Officer Dave Priestley explains how the company uses digital transformation, including an innovative member app, to deliver value and a superior customer experience. Despite initial challenges with legacy systems, Vitality has leveraged technology and partnerships, such as with TCS, to create a unified customer platform and adapt rapidly to new demands like the COVID-19 pandemic, all while focusing on customer-centric outcomes.

title: Spotify, Match Launch Coalition to Protest App Store Rules
summary: Spotify, Match Group, Epic Games, and 10 other organizations have formed the Coalition for App Fairness to challenge the app store rules of Apple and Google. The coalition introduced "App Store Principles," advocating against platform owners using developer data to compete and requiring exclusive use of their app stores or payment systems. This move aims to pressure Apple and Google into modifying their existing app store guidelines.

title: 3 quick reasons I like the IOO ETF
summary: The iShares Global 100 ETF (ASX: IOO) is recommended for its three key features: diversification from the Australian market, exposure to global developed and emerging markets, and investment in strong, growing businesses with entrenched economic moats. The article highlights its holdings in major global companies like Apple and Microsoft, and its 10-year average annual return of 13.1%. The author suggests it's a good option for investors seeking to diversify beyond ASX shares.

title: Texas Software Provider to Local Governments Reports Data Breach
summary: Tyler Technologies, a software provider for local governments and schools, announced a data breach affecting its internal network and phone systems. While the company stated that client data and hosted systems were not believed to be impacted, a cybersecurity expert warned of potential risks to customer passwords and suggested immediate password resets as a precaution. The incident is being investigated, and the FBI has been contacted.

title: Microsoft Teams telephony Survivable Branch Appliances (SBA)
summary: Microsoft announced that partners will offer Survivable Branch Appliances (SBAs) for Microsoft Teams telephony. These SBAs will enable telephony to function via a PSTN connection even when internet or Office 365 connectivity is lost, utilizing a new "Teams Offline mode." Ribbon and AudioCodes are among the first vendors to provide SBA support for Teams.

title: EM’s Weekly Roundup: Accenture Invests $3B to Establish Cloud Division; Veritas/DXC Health Deal to Close Oct. 1st; SAIC Reorganizing Business Structure; LTG Bruce Crawford Joins Rubrik Advisory Board; Collins Aerospace Receives $317M Contract
summary: This weekly roundup covers significant events in the government contracting and technology sectors. Key highlights include Accenture's $3 billion investment to form a new cloud division, Veritas Capital's impending $5 billion acquisition of DXC Technology's health business, and SAIC's reorganization to accelerate growth. Additionally, LTG Bruce Crawford joined Rubrik's advisory board, and Collins Aerospace secured a $317 million contract for radio communication systems.

title: Detecting VBA Process Hollowing With Cortex XDR
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has observed advanced VBA activity, specifically VBA-RunPE, which is an implementation of the RunPE technique allowing executables to run from memory in Microsoft Word and Excel to evade detection. Attackers use this process hollowing technique to hide malicious code inside legitimate processes and bypass application whitelisting. Cortex XDR, with its behavioral detectors and the latest Agent 7.2, provides protection against VBA-RunPE by identifying anomalous behavior like suspicious command-line arguments and unusual DLL loads by Office processes.

title: Yom Kippur marks the Jewish holiday of free speech
summary: This article discusses the concept of free speech within the context of the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur, drawing parallels to contemporary debates surrounding social media platforms and Section 230 of the U.S. Communications Decency Act. The author argues that while free speech is invaluable, it must have critical limits, especially concerning harmful content like fake news and hate speech. The piece suggests that regulations are needed to restrain offensive speech in a way that ultimately promotes genuine free speech rather than undermining it.

title: AiThority Interview with Chris Kozup, CMO at Aruba Networks (a Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company)
summary: Chris Kozup, CMO at Aruba, discusses his role, the challenges facing a CMO in the networking industry, and how Aruba is adapting its marketing strategies. He highlights the shift towards data at the Edge and the importance of digital engagement, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Kozup also shares insights on content formats, measuring marketing success, and the future of marketing in a post-COVID era, emphasizing a "Customer First, Customer Last" mindset.

title: HP Reverb G2: premium experience with cutting-edge technology by Jose Antunes - ProVideo Coalition
summary: The HP Reverb G2 VR headset is presented as the new standard for PC Virtual Reality, offering a premium and immersive experience with cutting-edge technology at an affordable price. It boasts the world's highest resolution among major vendors and has received updates to improve clarity and ease of use. The article positions it as a superior alternative to the discontinued Oculus Rift S and the untethered Oculus Quest 2, especially for users seeking a high-quality PCVR experience.

title: Humana And Salesforce Partner Up To Deliver More Personalized Care
summary: Humana and Salesforce have announced a multi-year partnership to enhance personalized care for Humana's 13 million customers. Utilizing Salesforce Health Cloud's new Enterprise Clinical Operating Model (ECOM), Humana aims to improve communication between patients, providers, and claims experts by integrating electronic health records. This collaboration seeks to digitize healthcare processes, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on virtual care.

title: Lenovo Expands Stylish ThinkBook Portfolio to Enhance New Working Models
summary: Lenovo has significantly expanded its ThinkBook portfolio, introducing six new models designed for modern professionals and the "work-from-anywhere" environment. The new lineup includes laptops like the ThinkBook 15 Gen 2 i with integrated wireless earbuds and the ThinkBook 14s Yoga i, a 2-in-1 model, alongside a new ThinkVision T27hv-20 USB-C Hub monitor. These devices emphasize enhanced collaboration, security features like Smart Guard, and intuitive software, catering to the evolving needs of small and medium businesses.

title: AI improves customer experience, call center efficiency
summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance customer experience and call center efficiency, especially given the increased interaction volume due to COVID-19. It highlights how AI can automate routine tasks, provide self-service options, and make agents more productive by offering personalized experiences and predictive analytics. The piece also details various forms of AI being adopted, such as predictive routing, sentiment analysis, and voice transcription, along with case studies demonstrating successful implementations and their benefits.

title: Worlds Inc. vs. Microsoft in Patent Infringement Lawsuit Related to “Minecraft”
summary: Worlds Inc. has filed a patent infringement complaint against Microsoft Corporation, alleging that its "Minecraft" video game product infringes on Worlds' U.S. Patent No. 8,082,501. This patent, related to 3D online virtual worlds, previously survived validity challenges against Activision Blizzard and Bungie Inc. Worlds Inc. seeks to enforce its intellectual property rights and secure compensation for its foundational technology.

title: EA Play games join Xbox Game Pass Ultimate in November
summary: EA Play's game library will officially be added to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on November 10, coinciding with the launch of the Xbox Series X and S. This integration brings 89 EA-published titles, 10 hours of free gameplay for select new EA releases, and a 10% discount on digital EA content to Ultimate subscribers. EA Play games will also become available for PC users in December and for Android mobile devices via xCloud.

title: Fiat Chrysler CEO MIke Manley will not be on Stellantis board after merger with Groupe PSA
summary: Fiat Chrysler CEO Mike Manley will not be joining the Stellantis board after the merger with Groupe PSA, despite the 50-50 stock split, as PSA will name six board members compared to FCA's five. Manley is expected to continue with Stellantis in a senior executive role, which has not yet been specified. The combined company, set to become the world's fourth-largest automaker, has announced 11 board members, including chairman John Elkann and CEO Carlos Tavares.

title: NatWest offers online banking customers free security services
summary: NatWest Group is partnering with Malwarebytes to offer its online banking customers free access to advanced endpoint protection services. This initiative comes in response to a significant increase in online banking fraud, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic, affecting both personal and business users. The service, available across all NatWest Group brands, allows customers to install Malwarebytes Premium on multiple devices to enhance their cyber security.

title: Campbell CIO: ERP modernization key to absorbing $5B acquisition
summary: Campbell Soup Company modernized its ERP system by migrating from Oracle to SAP HANA 2.0 to absorb the increased transactional volume from its nearly $5 billion acquisition of Snyder's-Lance. This incremental upgrade was crucial for real-time analytics, business continuity, and agility, especially during the pandemic-driven changes in consumer demand. The company plans a future transition to SAP S/4 HANA for advanced analytics.

title: Good story, bad investment
summary: Thematic ETFs often present compelling narratives around long-term trends like AI or electric vehicles, but Morningstar analyst Alex Bryan warns that a good story doesn't guarantee a sound investment. Investors must successfully bet on three factors: the macro trend playing out, the portfolio companies significantly benefiting, and the market not having already priced in the growth. Historically, most thematic ETFs underperform and many fail to survive long-term, making caution and thorough due diligence essential.

title: Microsoft named a leader in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Integration Platform as a Service
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in Gartner's 2020 Enterprise Integration Platform as a Service (EiPaaS) Magic Quadrant for the third consecutive year, based on its ability to execute and completeness of vision. The company's Azure Integration Services (AIS), including API Management, Logic Apps, Service Bus, and Event Grid, offers extensive integration capabilities with over 370 connectors. AIS is used by over 40,000 customers globally, including more than 60 percent of Fortune 500 companies.

title: Delivering 3D Creators' Visions to Customers the Way They Intended
summary: Sony has developed the Eye-sensing Light Field Display (ELFD) to overcome the limitations of conventional 3D displays by offering a glasses-free, high-definition 3D experience with real-time eye-tracking and rendering. This technology aims to accurately reproduce creators' 3D visions and is being explored for applications in product design, entertainment, and various B2B fields, with ongoing efforts to expand its capabilities for larger systems and multiple viewers.

title: IonQ Unveils World's Most Powerful Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has revealed its next-generation quantum computer, featuring 32 "perfect qubits" and an expected quantum volume exceeding 4,000,000. This new system, which boasts improved fidelity and is built on decades of research, will be available through Amazon Braket and Microsoft's Azure Quantum. IonQ aims to significantly increase its qubit count annually, with two more generations of hardware already in development.

title: Introducing the World’s Most Powerful Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has unveiled its new quantum computer, which is described as the most powerful on the market, featuring 32 perfect qubits and a quantum volume of at least 4,000,000. This development validates IonQ's trapped-ion approach and positions quantum computing as the next major technological revolution, with the potential to transform numerous industries and create trillions in economic value. The system will initially be available to partners via private beta, then commercially on AWS Braket and Microsoft Azure Quantum in early 2021, aiming to accelerate the adoption and development of quantum applications.

title: The Most Popular ESG ETF is also a Five-Star Fund
summary: The iShares ESG Aware MSCI USA ETF (ESGU), a five-star rated fund by CFRA, is highlighted for its strong record and appealing holdings. Despite excluding some companies based on ESG criteria, ESGU has outperformed the S&P 500 Index over various periods and maintains a sector exposure similar to the broader market. CFRA recommends ESGU for investors seeking ESG-focused strategies, citing its low expense ratio and growing popularity.

title: Videogame Stocks Have Soared for 20 Years. They’re About to Get Another Boost.
summary: The article discusses the upcoming launch of new videogame consoles, Microsoft's Xbox Series X and Sony's PlayStation 5, which are expected to boost videogame stocks. Despite pandemic-related delays in other industries, these major consumer events are proceeding on schedule. The piece highlights the past strong performance of videogame stocks and anticipates further growth with the new console generation.

title: IonQ Unveils New 32-Qubit Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has unveiled a new 32-qubit quantum computer with low gate errors, expecting a quantum volume greater than 4,000,000. This new system features perfect atomic clock qubits and random access all-to-all gate operations, and will be available via private beta before commercial release on Amazon Braket and Microsoft's Azure Quantum. IonQ plans to continue rapidly increasing qubit count and improving fidelity, with two new generations of hardware already in development.

title: Birthday week: Cloudflare turns 10
summary: Cloudflare celebrated its 10th birthday with a "Birthday Week" featuring several significant announcements. Key updates included advancements in their Workers platform with Durable Objects and Cron Triggers, a new privacy-focused Web Analytics product, and the launch of Cloudflare Radar for real-time internet traffic insights. The company also introduced API enhancements like gRPC support and API Shield, and Automatic Platform Optimization for improved website performance, starting with WordPress.

title: Larry Ellison's TikTok bid puts Oracle chairman back in the spotlight
summary: Oracle Corp. co-founder Larry Ellison's pursuit of a deal with TikTok could significantly boost Oracle's cloud-computing business and put him back in the tech industry spotlight. The proposed deal involves Oracle and Walmart Inc. taking a combined 20% stake in a new U.S.-based TikTok, with Oracle guaranteeing the security of U.S. user data. This move is seen as a way for Oracle to gain traction against market leaders like Amazon and Microsoft in the cloud computing sector, an area Ellison once dismissed.

title: A.I. gets down in the dirt as precision agriculture takes off
summary: Artificial intelligence is becoming a crucial tool in agriculture, helping farmers to significantly boost yields, minimize waste, and reduce pollution. Companies like Deere & Co. are integrating A.I. into their machinery for real-time adjustments during harvest, while startups like Ceres Imaging offer data-driven insights through aerial imaging to optimize resource use. This shift towards precision agriculture promises substantial cost savings and increased farmer incomes by improving efficiency and reducing environmental impact.

title: NVIDIA Introduces New Family of BlueField DPUs to Bring Breakthrough Networking, Storage and Security Performance to Every Data Center
summary: NVIDIA has announced a new family of Data Processing Units (DPUs) called BlueField, accompanied by the DOCA software development kit, to enhance networking, storage, and security performance in data centers. These DPUs offload critical tasks from CPUs, thereby freeing up processing power for other enterprise applications. Major server manufacturers and software partners like VMware, Red Hat, and Canonical are integrating NVIDIA DPUs into their offerings.

title: Microsoft announces plans for first datacenter region in Greece as part of “GR for GRowth” digital transformation initiative
summary: Microsoft has announced its "GR for GRowth" initiative, which includes plans to build its first datacenter region in Greece and skill 100,000 people in digital technologies by 2025. This significant investment aims to accelerate the digitization of Greece's public sector and businesses, providing access to local cloud services and fostering economic growth. The initiative reflects Microsoft's confidence in Greece's future and its commitment to being a technology ally for the country's development.

title: Why does Microsoft have an office at the UN? A Q&A with the company’s UN lead – On the Issues
summary: Microsoft established a United Nations Affairs office in New York City to deepen its engagement with the UN on global issues like human rights, environmental sustainability, and digital empowerment. John Frank, Vice President of UN Affairs, explains that this initiative aims to foster multi-stakeholder collaborations to tackle pressing global challenges. The office focuses on building relationships, making Microsoft's partnerships more impactful, and helping the UN leverage technology for its missions.

title: Microsoft Corp. adds two West Des Moines data centers, five in all
summary: Microsoft is expanding its data center operations in West Des Moines by adding two new facilities, bringing its total to five in the city. The projects, each estimated to cost between $1-2 billion and employ 50-75 workers, are expected to break ground next September and open their first buildings in late 2022. The decision to expand is driven by growing demand for cloud computing and strategic considerations like skilled labor, fiber optic access, and reliable power.

title: Rockwell Automation and Microsoft Expand Partnership to Simplify Industrial Transformation
summary: Rockwell Automation and Microsoft have expanded their partnership with a five-year agreement to develop integrated, market-ready solutions for industrial customers. This collaboration aims to enhance digital agility through cloud technology, combining their expertise to help manufacturers save on infrastructure costs, speed time-to-value, and increase productivity. The partnership focuses on delivering innovative edge-to-cloud solutions that connect information seamlessly between development, operations, and maintenance teams, thereby removing data silos and accelerating industrial digital transformation.

title: HireVue acquires recruiting chatbot startup AllyO
summary: HireVue, a video interviewing vendor, has acquired AllyO, a startup specializing in chatbot technology for high-volume hiring. AllyO's conversational chatbots automate parts of the recruiting process, such as providing job information and conducting initial interviews. This acquisition aims to integrate AllyO's technology with HireVue's platform to enhance talent engagement and streamline the hiring process for companies.

title: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses AI, data centers, getting acquired by Nvidia and more
summary: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses the 2020 acquisition by Nvidia for $40 billion, highlighting the strategic alignment of both companies in AI and data centers. He emphasizes that the merger will accelerate Arm's trajectory into new markets like automotive and data centers, while also expanding their IP offerings. Segars addresses regulatory hurdles and concerns about licensing to Chinese companies, asserting that the deal is pro-competitive and will not alter Arm's licensing approach.

title: Rockwell Automation and Microsoft expand partnership to simplify industrial transformation
summary: Rockwell Automation and Microsoft have announced a five-year expanded partnership to simplify industrial transformation. The collaboration focuses on developing integrated, market-ready solutions leveraging cloud technology to improve digital agility for industrial customers. This partnership aims to connect development, operations, and maintenance teams through a singular, trusted data environment, enabling digital prototyping, secure data sharing, and accelerated innovation.

title: SAP® SuccessFactors® Employee Central Tops 4,000 Customers
summary: SAP announced its SuccessFactors® Employee Central solution has surpassed 4,000 customers, indicating its rapid growth as a core HR solution. The cloud-based Human Experience Management (HXM) suite offers global scalability, supporting 42 languages and over 2,000 regulatory changes annually for 99 countries. Customers praise the platform for streamlining HR processes, improving employee engagement, and enabling data-driven decisions.

title: IonQ Releases A New 32-Qubit Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer With Massive Quantum Volume Claims
summary: IonQ has released its 5th generation 32-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer, claiming an astounding quantum volume of 4 million, significantly higher than previously published records. While the company calculated this figure rather than running quantum volume circuits, they anticipate a research paper confirming the performance. This development marks a significant advancement in quantum computing, with plans for private betas and cloud platform deployment in 2021.

title: 2020 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms: Key Takeaways
summary: This article provides key takeaways from Gartner's 2020 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms, highlighting the growing importance of LCAPs due to application delivery challenges and developer shortages. It details Gartner's definition of LCAPs, projected adoption rates, typical use cases, and evaluates 18 providers across the niche players, challengers, visionaries, and leaders quadrants, noting specific strengths and new additions.

title: Damco Solutions added monday.com to its partnership pool to prioritize workplace transformation
summary: Damco Solutions Inc. has announced a partnership with monday.com, a SaaS-based collaboration and productivity platform, to help businesses create future-ready digital workplaces. This strategic alliance aims to simplify project management and supercharge workforces with custom workflows, easy collaboration, automation, real-time reporting, and integrations. The partnership leverages Damco's IT services expertise and monday.com's platform to drive transformational experiences for global teams, especially expanding monday.com's presence in North America.

title: Private equity giant Blackstone set to open tech office in Miami
summary: Private equity firm Blackstone plans to open a technology-focused headquarters in Miami, creating up to 215 tech jobs with an average salary of $200,000. Miami-Dade County will provide up to $650,000 in job incentives, anticipating $910,303 in new tax revenue. This move signifies Miami's growing appeal as a tech hub, attracting other companies like Google, Microsoft, and Softbank.

title: IBM to break up 109-year old firm to focus on high-margin cloud computing
summary: IBM is splitting into two public companies, spinning off its IT infrastructure services unit to focus on high-margin cloud computing. This strategic move, spearheaded by CEO Arvind Krishna, aims to streamline the 109-year-old firm, allowing the remaining entity to concentrate on its software and solutions portfolio. The company expects to incur $2.5 billion in expenses related to the spin-off and projects Q3 revenue of $17.6 billion and an adjusted profit per share of $2.58.

title: GameStop announces multiyear strategic partnership with Microsoft
summary: GameStop Corp. announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Microsoft Corp. to advance its physical and digital video game offerings and enhance its retail technology infrastructure. The partnership will see GameStop standardize its business operations on Microsoft's cloud solutions and hardware, including Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Surface devices, to create a premier omni-channel gaming destination. It also expands GameStop's Xbox product offerings to include Xbox All Access, benefiting both companies in customer acquisition and lifetime revenue.

title: QQQ’s Stellar ETF Rise
summary: The article discusses the enduring success of the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ETF despite criticisms of its underlying Nasdaq-100 index structure. It highlights QQQ's significant asset growth, strong performance against major indices, and its appeal to investors seeking exposure to tech and growth stocks, particularly among younger generations. The piece also delves into the unique rules and rebalancing methodology of the Nasdaq-100 and QQQ's substantial marketing efforts.

title: Videogames are about to get more expensive for the first time in 15 years
summary: Videogame prices are set to increase for the first time in 15 years, with new top-tier games for next-generation consoles priced at $70. This change coincides with the release of new Xbox and PlayStation consoles, affecting titles from publishers like Take-Two Interactive Software Inc., Microsoft Corp., and Sony Corp.

title: Foreign cloud service providers led by Amazon, MS play big in Korea
